opportunity.title: Cross-channel bug report triage for small teams
opportunity.one_line_summary: Small teams lose customer bug reports that arrive through several channels and want one place to triage them.

verdict_rationale.text: Several independent discussions describe the same pain, but the sample is small and shows little proof that teams would pay.
verdict_rationale.rationale: Nine discussions and one payment quote support further validation, not a build commitment.

problem_statement.text: Teams report that bug reports arrive in issue trackers, email and chat and that duplicates and lost reports are common.

affected_users.text: Maintainers and support leads on teams of two to ten people who triage reports by hand.
affected_users.validation: Ask five maintainers how many channels they check and how they de-duplicate.

how_it_falls_short.text: Manual tracking is likely to drift out of date as report volume grows.
how_it_falls_short.validation: Observe two teams for a week.

thesis.text: The same triage pain is described independently on two different sources.

counter_thesis.text: Growth over time could not be computed, so it is unknown whether interest is rising.
counter_thesis.missing_information: Discussion counts per month for at least three months.

interpretation.text: Independent discussions across more than one source suggest the problem is not confined to one community.
interpretation.rationale: Breadth across sources lowers the chance of a single-community quirk.

summary.text: Only a single payment-related quote was found, which is not enough to say teams would pay.
summary.missing_information: Direct statements of budget or current spend from the target personas.

evidence_gaps.description: No evidence of how much teams spend today on triage tooling.
evidence_gaps.impact: Pricing cannot be anchored to anything observed.
evidence_gaps.how_to_close: Run five consent-based interviews and ask about current tools and budget.

evidence_gaps.description: Growth rate could not be computed from the collected window.
evidence_gaps.impact: Unknown whether the problem is growing or shrinking.
evidence_gaps.how_to_close: Collect at least three months of data before relying on trend claims.

personas.name: The overloaded maintainer
personas.context: Works in a team of two to ten and receives bug reports from several places.
goals: See every report in one list
Avoid answering the same report twice

frustrations.text: Reports are scattered and easy to miss.

current_workaround.text: Copying reports into a shared spreadsheet by hand.

positioning.text: A lightweight inbox that merges bug reports from a few channels and flags duplicates.
positioning.rationale: Narrow scope keeps the first build small.

value_proposition.text: Fewer lost and duplicated reports for small teams without adopting a heavy support suite.
value_proposition.validation: Landing-page test with two positioning variants.

differentiation.text: Designed for teams of two to ten and for bug reports rather than general helpdesk tickets.
differentiation.validation: Compare against two named alternatives in interviews.

capabilities.name: Unified inbox
capabilities.description: Collect reports from connected channels into one list.

capabilities.name: Duplicate flagging
capabilities.description: Suggest likely duplicates for a human to confirm.

capabilities.name: Assignment and status
capabilities.description: Assign a report and track its status.

non_goals: Automatic closing of reports without a human

success_metrics.name: Weekly active teams
success_metrics.how_measured: Count teams that triage at least 10 reports in a week

success_metrics.name: Duplicate acceptance rate
success_metrics.target: At least 50 percent of flagged duplicates confirmed
success_metrics.how_measured: Confirm or reject actions on suggestions

features.name: Email forwarding intake
features.description: A forwarding address turns each email into a report.
features.user_value: Reports from email land in the list.

justification.text: Email is one of the channels named in the discussions.

features.name: Issue tracker import
features.description: Read-only import of issues from one tracker.
features.user_value: Existing tracker issues appear in the same list.

justification.text: A public issue tracker is a channel named in the discussions.

features.name: Duplicate suggestions
features.description: Show similar reports and let a person merge them.

justification.text: One maintainer says duplicate reports take up much of their morning.

features.name: Assignment and status
features.description: Assign an owner and set a status.

justification.text: Common triage practice; not directly evidenced in the excerpts.
justification.rationale: Needed for the inbox to be usable day to day.

exclusions.name: Chat channel integrations
exclusions.reason: Each integration adds maintenance; validate email and tracker first.
exclusions.revisit_when: Pilot teams ask for a specific chat tool

exclusions.name: Automatic merging
exclusions.reason: A wrong merge loses information; keep a human in the loop.
exclusions.revisit_when: Duplicate acceptance rate is consistently high

scope_assessment.team_assumption: One part-time developer, experienced with TypeScript and PostgreSQL
scope_assessment.complexity_notes: Assumes the four listed MVP features; duplicate suggestions are the riskiest part. Email forwarding and tracker API access are dependencies, and provider onboarding or scope growth could change the range.

journeys.name: Triage a new report
journeys.goal: Decide what to do with a new report in under a minute

steps.action: A report arrives by email or from the tracker
steps.system_response: The report is added to the inbox
Show up to three likely duplicates

steps.action: Merge a duplicate or keep the report separate
Assign an owner and set a status

failure_modes: A merge is applied to the wrong report

architecture.summary: One web application with a background worker for intake, kept in a single repository and deployable as one unit.

components.name: Intake worker
components.responsibility: Process forwarded email and import issues

tech_choices.rationale: Matches the preferred stack and the solo developer's skills.

alternatives.name: Server-rendered pages
alternatives.why_not_chosen: A live inbox benefits from client-side updates.

tech_choices.trade_offs: A larger client bundle in exchange for a responsive inbox.

tech_choices.rationale: One language across the stack lowers cognitive load.

alternatives.name: Python
alternatives.why_not_chosen: Adds a second language for one developer.

tech_choices.trade_offs: Less convenient for later text-similarity experiments.

tech_choices.rationale: Relational data with simple text search is enough for the MVP.

alternatives.name: Document database
alternatives.why_not_chosen: Reports, teams and assignments are relational.

alternatives.name: Self-built accounts
alternatives.why_not_chosen: More security surface for no MVP benefit.

integrations.name: Inbound email forwarding
integrations.failure_handling: Keep the raw message, retry, and alert an admin after repeated failures.

non_functional.requirement: Store only what is needed from forwarded messages
non_functional.approach: Keep subject and body text, drop attachments, allow deletion per team.
Row-level access rules keyed on team membership.

non_functional.target: No lost reports during a single worker restart
non_functional.approach: Persist the message before processing and process idempotently.

decisions.title: Single deployable unit versus separate services
decisions.context: One part-time developer must ship and operate everything.
decisions.consequences: Fast to build; revisit if intake load grows by an order of magnitude.

decisions.title: Duplicate detection method
decisions.context: A simple, explainable method is preferred for the first version.

options.name: Embedding service
cons: Extra cost and a new dependency

decisions.consequences: Accept lower accuracy and measure the duplicate acceptance rate before investing more.

architecture.deployment_notes: One web service and one worker on a managed platform with a managed PostgreSQL instance; environments for staging and production.

database.tenancy_rationale: Reports belong to a team and every query is scoped to the caller's team memberships.
